b. One-hour structural frame or heavy timber.
c. Heavy timber floor/ceiling/roof assemblies.
(8) Type V-A—Protected wood frame (commonly used in the construction of newer apartment buildings; there is no exposed wood visible).
a. One-hour exterior walls.
b. One-hour structural frame.
c. One-hour floor/ceiling/roof.
(9) Type V-B—Unprotected wood frame (examples of Type V-N construction are single-family homes and garages. They often have exposed wood so there is no fire resistance). Note exceptions in the building code for fire resistance ratings of exterior walls and opening protection.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 3(2))
394:
This is for administration and enforcement of state minimum standard codes for construction adopted and amended by the DCA. Said codes shall be referred to as "the codes."
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(1))
395:
(a) General. These codes are declared to be remedial, and shall be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes thereof - public safety, health, and general welfare - through structural strength, stability, sanitation, adequate light and ventilation, and safety to life and property from fire and other hazards including alteration, repair, removal, demolition, use, and occupancy of buildings, structures, or premises, and by regulating installation and maintenance of all electrical, gas, mechanical, sprinkler and plumbing systems, referred to as service systems or systems. The term "building" includes all structures.
(b) Quality control. Quality control of materials and workmanship is not within the purview of the construction codes except as it relates to the purposes stated therein.
(c) Permitting and inspection. The inspection or permitting of any building, system, or plan, under the requirements of the codes shall not be construed in any court as a warranty of the physical condition of such building, system or plan or their adequacy. Neither the city, nor any employee, shall be liable for damages for any defect or hazardous or illegal condition or inadequacy in such building, system or plan, nor for any failure of any component of such, which may occur subsequent to such inspection or permitting.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(2))
396:
(a) Applicability.
(1) General. Where, in any case, different sections of these codes specify different materials, methods of construction, or other requirements, the most restrictive shall govern. Where there is a conflict between a general requirement and a specific requirement, the specific shall be applicable. The Watkinsville City Code, to the extent more specific, stringent or restrictive, will prevail over any code incorporated by reference, including, without limitation, the Georgia State Minimum Standard Codes, the International Existing Building Code and the International Property Maintenance Code.
(2) Building. The International Building Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to construction, alteration, repair, equipment, use and occupancy, location, maintenance, removal, and demolition, of every building or structure or any appurtenances connected or attached to such buildings or structures, except one- and two-family dwellings.
(3) Electrical. The National Electrical Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to electrical systems, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances thereto.
(4) Gas. The International Fuel Gas Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to gas piping, gas appliances, and related accessories as covered in this Code. These requirements apply to gas piping systems from point of delivery to inlet connections of appliances and installation and operation of residential and commercial gas appliances and related accessories, except one- and two-family dwellings.
(5) Mechanical. The International Mechanical Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to mechanical systems, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings and/or appurtenances, including ventilating, heating, cooling, air conditioning and refrigeration systems, incinerators, and other energy related systems, except one- and two-family dwellings.
(6) Plumbing. The International Plumbing Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to all plumbing, including alterations, repairs, replacement, equipment, appliances, fixtures, fittings, and appurtenances, and when connected to water or sewer.
(7) One- and two-family dwellings and their accessory structures. In addition to the codes herein, the International Residential Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, applies to building, mechanical, and gas systems in new one- and two-family dwellings and their accessory buildings, plus additions, alterations, renovations and repairs of existing dwellings.
(8) Energy. The International Energy Conservation Code, adopted and amended by the DCA, regulates the design of building envelopes for adequate thermal resistance and low air leakage and the design and selection of mechanical, electrical, service water heating, and illumination systems and equipment that will enable effective use of energy in new construction.
(b) Federal and state authority. The codes shall not be held to deprive any federal or state agency, or any applicable governing authority having jurisdiction, of any power or authority it had on the effective date of the adoption of the construction codes or of any remedy then existing for the enforcement of its orders, nor shall it deprive any individual or entity of its legal rights as provided by law.
(c) Appendices. Appendices referenced are an integral part of the codes.
(d) Referenced standards. Standards referenced in the construction codes shall be considered an integral part of the codes. If specific portions of a standard are denoted by code text, only those portions of the standard shall be enforced. Where code provisions conflict with a standard, the code provisions shall be enforced.
(e) Maintenance. All buildings, structures, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems, existing and new, and all parts thereof, shall be maintained in a safe and sanitary condition. All devices or safeguards required by the codes when constructed, altered, or repaired, shall be maintained in good working order. The owner, or designated agent, shall be responsible for maintenance of buildings and all systems.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(3))
397:
(a) General. Alterations, repairs, or rehabilitation work may be made to any existing structure, building, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing system without requiring the building, structure, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, or gas system to comply with all the requirements of the codes, if the alteration, repair, or rehabilitation work conforms to the requirements of the codes for new construction. The building official shall determine the extent to which the existing system shall be made to conform to the requirements of the codes for new construction.
(b) Change of occupancy. If the occupancy classification of any existing building or structure is changed, the building, electrical, gas, mechanical, and plumbing systems shall be made to conform to the codes as required by the building official.
(c) Special historic buildings. The codes shall not be mandatory for existing buildings or structures identified and classified by the state or city as historic buildings when such are judged by the building official to be safe and in the public interest of health, safety, and welfare regarding any proposed work.
(d) Maintenance and repair. Owners shall not allow structures to deteriorate by failing to provide maintenance and repair. Decay, deterioration and structural defects, jeopardize structural integrity and pose hazards. All structures shall be kept free from the following structural defects and conditions. Owners shall maintain and repair such owners' structures as to not endanger the property with the following violations which jeopardize structural integrity:
(1) Foundations. Foundations shall support the structure as originally constructed, and be free of deterioration, holes, cracks and buckling.
(2) Structural member violations. Defective or deteriorated floor supports, or structural members of insufficient size to carry loads safely. Members of walls, partitions or other vertical supports that split, lean, list or buckle due to defective material or deterioration. Structural members of ceilings and roofs, or other horizontal structural members, which sag, split or buckle or are of insufficient size to carry imposed loads with safety. Interior staircases shall be maintained in good repair.
(3) Exterior surfaces and materials violations. Floors, walls and roofs having holes, cracks and loose, warped, protruding or rotting boards or any other condition admitting moisture or other elements. Exterior surfaces improperly exposed to the weather, which shall be repaired and weatherproofed to protect from further deterioration. Masonry joints shall be maintained. Fireplaces or chimneys which list, bulge or settle or are of insufficient size or strength to carry loads with safety. Such shall be maintained/repaired to as to be in good repair.
(4) Weather protection, ventilation. Lack of weather protection, or a fault or defect which renders it unsafe or not weathertight, are violations. Windows, exterior doors and siding shall be watertight. Flashing, including at chimneys, doors, and windows, shall be in good repair. Downspouts and gutters shall be maintained so rain runoff is directed away from the structure. Foundation and attic vents shall be maintained to ventilate the crawl and attic spaces.
(5) Stairways, porches and appurtenances. Exterior staircases, porches and appurtenances thereto shall be maintained in good repair.
(6) Rodent, termite infestation. Structures shall be free of wood boring insects and rodents.
(7) Security and utilities. Unoccupied buildings shall be secured to prevent intrusion, and utilities shall be properly disconnected.
(8) Dependencies, additional site features. Tree limbs shall be trimmed away, and tree roots cleared away from foundations. Soil erosion and deposition shall not be allowed to endanger structures.
(e) Permit; bond.
(1) It shall be unlawful for any person to relocate a building, house or similar structure without having first obtained from the city a permit therefor and having paid the required fee for the issuance of said permit.
(2) Upon the issuance of a permit, the holder thereof shall post with the city clerk either a cash bond in the amount of $1,000.00 or a letter of credit from a banking institution, authorized by the state to provide banking services, upon the following conditions:
a. The bond or letter of credit shall be returned to the holder upon satisfactory completion of the project.
b. Should the project remain unfinished, kept in an unsafe manner, or should the holder fail to clear the lot of all debris and materials within the time specified on the permit, the city manager or a designated agent shall have authority to notify the holder of the permit that the city shall complete the project in a satisfactory manner at the permit holder's expense.
c. If the expense is less than the bond posted or identified in the letter of credit, the remainder shall be returned to the permit holder.
d. If the cost is greater than the bond or letter of credit, such difference shall be due and payable to the city, and upon authorization by the city council, shall be assessed against the property.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(4); Ord. of 10-21-2020, § 1)
398:
(a) Creation of building department. There is established the building department and the person in charge (and designees) shall be known as the building official. The city shall establish the qualifications for the building official and other code enforcement personnel. The duties of the department may be contracted out in full to a third-party entity.
(b) Restrictions on employees. An officer or employee connected with the department shall not be financially interested in the furnishing of labor, material, or appliances for the construction, alteration, or maintenance of a building, structure, service, system, or in the making of plans or of specifications thereof, unless such department officer or employee is the owner of such. This officer or employee shall not engage in any other work which is inconsistent with such officer's or employee's duties or conflict with the interests of the department.
(c) Records. The building official shall keep a record of the business of the department. The records shall be open to public inspection per O.C.G.A. tit. 50, ch. 18, art. 4 (O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70 et seq.).
(d) Liability. Any officer or employee, acting for the city in the discharge of duties, shall not thereby be personally liable, and is relieved from personal liability, for any damage that may occur as a result of any good faith act required or permitted in the discharge of duties. Any suit against them because of such good faith act performed in the enforcement of the codes shall be defended by the city until the final termination of the proceedings.
(e) Reports. The building official shall submit a report each year covering the work of the building department during the preceding year, and may incorporate a summary of the decisions during said year.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(5))
399:
(a) General. The building official or city council's designee is authorized and directed to enforce the codes and interpret the codes consistent with their intent and purpose. The city may contract with a third party to provide the duties of the building official.
(b) Right of entry.
(1) When necessary to make an inspection, or when the building official has reasonable cause to believe there exists a condition or code violation which makes such building, structure, premises, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems unsafe, dangerous, or hazardous, the building official may enter at all reasonable times to inspect or to perform any duty imposed on the building official by these codes, but if such is occupied, such official shall first present proper credentials and request entry. If such is unoccupied, the building official shall first make a reasonable effort to locate the owner or other persons having control and request entry. If entry is refused, the building official shall have recourse to every remedy under law to secure entry.
(2) When the building official shall have first obtained a proper inspection warrant or other remedy provided by law to secure entry, no owner or occupant or any other persons having control shall fail or neglect, after proper request is made as herein provided, to promptly permit entry therein by the building official for inspection and examination pursuant to the construction codes.
(c) Stop-work orders. Upon notice from the building official, work on any building or system contrary to the codes or in a dangerous or unsafe manner, shall immediately cease. Notice shall be in writing and given to the owner of the property, or agent, or the person doing the work, and shall state conditions under which work may be resumed. In an emergency, the building official shall not be required to give a written notice prior to stopping work.
(d) Revocation of permits.
(1) Misrepresentation of application. The building official may revoke a permit or approval, issued under the codes, if there has been a false statement or misrepresentation of material fact in the application or plans.
(2) Violation. The building official may revoke a permit upon determination that the construction, erection, alteration, repair, moving, demolition, installation or replacement of the building, structure, electrical, gas, mechanical, or plumbing systems is in violation of, or not in conformity with, the codes.
(e) Unsafe buildings or systems. All buildings or systems which are unsafe, unsanitary, or do not provide adequate egress, or which constitute a fire hazard, or are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use, constitute a hazard to safety or health, are considered unsafe buildings or service systems.
(f) Requirements not covered by Code. Any requirements necessary for strength, stability, or proper operation of a building or system, or for the public safety, health, and general welfare, not covered by the codes, shall be determined by the building official.
(g) Alternates. The codes are not to prevent use of a material or method not specifically prescribed by them, if such alternate has been approved by the building official, who shall approve such alternate, if it is at least the equivalent of that prescribed in the codes, in quality, strength, effectiveness, fire resistance, durability, and safety. The building official shall require sufficient evidence to substantiate any claim regarding the alternate.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(6))
400:
(a) Permit application.
(1) Required. Anyone who desires to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, change occupancy of, remove, convert, or replace a building or system regulated by the codes, shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permit, and in the case of demolition of a structure older than 50 years, from city council. A permit shall only be issued to a licensed contractor, or an owner of a residential structure being altered.
(2) Work authorized. A building or system permit gives the right to construct or install the work shown in the drawings and specifications with the application. If not on said drawings and specifications, separate permits shall be required.
(3) Minor repairs. Minor repairs less than $5,000.00, and roof replacement, siding and trim repair and gutter replacement, may be made with approval of the building official without a permit, if such repairs do not violate any codes.
(4) Information. Each application, with required fee, shall be filed with the building official on the form and contain a general description of the work. The application shall be signed by the owner, or authorized agent. It shall indicate the proposed occupancy of all parts of the building and of that portion of the site or lot not covered by the building, and contain other information required by the building official.
(5) Time. An incomplete application shall be deemed abandoned six months after the date of application. One or more extensions, not more than 90 days each, may be allowed by the building official, if requested in writing and justifiable cause is demonstrated.
(b) Drawings and specifications.
(1) Requirements. When required by the building official, two or more copies of specifications and scale drawings, with sufficient clarity and detail to indicate the work, shall accompany the application. Such shall contain information, notes or otherwise, as to quality of materials, where quality is essential to conformity with the codes. Such shall be specific, and the codes shall not be cited as a whole or in part, nor shall the term "legal" or its equivalent be used, as a substitute for specific information. All information, drawings, specifications and accompanying data shall bear the name and signature of the person responsible for the design.
(2) Additional data. The building official may require details, computations, stress diagrams, and other data necessary to describe the construction and the basis of calculations. All drawings, specifications, and data required by the building official to be prepared by an architect or engineer shall be affixed with such architect's or engineer's official seal.
(3) Design professional. The design professional shall be an architect or engineer legally registered in the state and shall affix such design professional's official seal to said drawings, specifications, and accompanying data, for all Group A, E, and I occupancies; buildings and structures three stories or more high; buildings and structures 5,000 square feet or more in area. For all other buildings and structures, the submittal shall bear the certification of the applicant that some specific state law exception permits its preparation by a person not so registered. Exception: Single-family dwellings and their accessory buildings, regardless of size, shall require neither a registered architect nor engineer, nor a certification that an architect or engineer is not required.
(4) Structural and fire resistance integrity. Plans for all buildings shall indicate how required structural and fire resistance integrity will be maintained where a penetration of a required fire resistance wall, floor, or partition will be made for conduits, pipes, and systems and indicate in sufficient detail how the fire integrity will be maintained where required fire resistance floors intersect the exterior walls.
(5) Site drawings. Drawings shall show the location of the proposed structure and every existing structure on the lot. The building official may require a boundary line survey prepared by a qualified surveyor.
(6) Hazardous occupancies. The building official may require the following:
a. Site plan. A general site plan of legible scale with location of all buildings, exterior storage facilities, permanent accessways, evacuation routes, parking lots, internal roads, chemical loading areas, equipment cleaning areas, storm and sanitary sewer accesses, emergency equipment, and adjacent property uses. The exterior storage areas shall be identified with the hazard classes and the maximum quantities per hazard class of hazardous materials stored.
b. Floor plan. A floor plan of legible scale with all hazardous materials storage facilities in the building, to indicate rooms, doorways, corridors, exits, fire rated assemblies with hourly rating, liquid-tight rooms, and evacuation routes. Each hazardous materials storage facility shall be identified with the hazard classes and quantity range per hazard class or the hazardous materials stored.
(c) Examination of documents; plan review. The building official shall examine each application and documents, drawings, specifications, computations, and additional data, and ascertain whether the construction described is in accordance with all codes, laws and ordinances.
(d) Issuing permits.
(1) Action. The building official shall act on an application without unreasonable or unnecessary delay. If the building official is satisfied the work described in an application and the documents conforms to the codes and laws and ordinances, such official shall issue a permit.
(2) Refusal to issue. If the application and the documents do not conform to the codes or other laws or ordinances, the building official shall not issue a permit, but shall return the documents to the applicant with such official's refusal to issue such permit. Such refusal shall, when requested, be in writing and contain the reason for refusal.
(3) Foundation permit. When application for permit to erect or enlarge a building is pending, the building official may issue a permit for foundation only. The holder is proceeding at such holder's own risk and without assurance that a permit for the remainder of the work will be granted or that corrections will not be required to meet the codes.
(4) Right-of-way. A permit shall not be given for construction or alteration of a building as to affect the exterior walls, bays, balconies, or other appendages or projections fronting on a street, alley, or public lane, or the placing on any lot or premises of any building or structure removed from another lot or premises, unless applicant has made application for and received approval of such; it is the duty of the building official to see that street lines are not encroached on.
(e) Contractor responsibilities. Every contractor shall comply with all state and local rules and regulations the city has adopted. If the state requires a state license, the contractor shall supply the city with such contractor's license number before receiving a permit for work.
(f) Conditions of permit.
(1) Intent. A permit is a license to proceed with work, not authority to violate any codes. Nor shall issuance of a permit prevent the building official from requiring a correction of errors in plans, construction, or violations of the codes. If work is not commenced within six months, or is suspended or abandoned for six months, the permit shall become invalid. Written extensions of time, requested in writing, not more than 90 days each, may be allowed for justifiable cause demonstrated.
(2) Affidavit. When a permit is issued in reliance on an affidavit or the work is, in the opinion of the building official, hazardous or complex, the architect/engineer who signed the affidavit or prepared the plans shall supervise such work. Such architect/engineer shall be responsible for conformity with the permit, provide contemporaneous inspection reports, and upon completion, file with the building official an affidavit that the work has been done in conformity with the plans and codes. If such architect/engineer is not available, the owner shall employ in such architect's or engineer's place a competent person/agency whose qualifications are approved by the building official.
(3) Plans. When the building official issues a permit, the building official shall notate both sets of plans "reviewed for code compliance." One set shall be retained by the building official and the other returned to the applicant. The plans shall be kept at the work site and shall be open to inspection by the building official.
(g) Fees.
(1) Prescribed fees. A permit shall not issue until the city fees have been paid. Nor shall there be an amendment to a permit until any additional fee is paid.
(2) Work before permit. Any person who commences work before obtaining the permits shall be penalized 100 percent of the permit fee in addition to the permit fees.
(3) Accounting. The building official shall keep an accurate accounting of all money collected, who paid, and the date thereof.
(4) Schedule of fees. On all work requiring a permit, a fee for each permit in the amount established by resolution shall be paid as required at the time of application.
(5) Valuations. Construction valuations shall be determined by size and type of the structure by reference to the building valuation data established from time-to-time by the International Code Council, and adjusted locally based on a square foot basis for the most recent median sales of new single-family construction built over the past two years, as reported by the county tax assessor.
(h) Inspections.
(1) Existing buildings. Before issuing a permit, the building official may examine a building or system for which application has been received, and inspect all buildings and systems, during and upon completion of work, and record such and all violations.
(2) Manufacturers and fabricators. The building official may inspect materials or assemblies at point of manufacture/fabrication, and record such and all violations.
(3) Inspection service. The building official may make the inspections required by subsection (h)(6) of this section and accept reports of recognized inspectors if such building official is satisfied as to such inspectors' qualifications. A certificate called for by the codes shall not be based on such reports unless in writing and certified by a responsible inspector.
(4) Inspections prior to certificate of occupancy (C.O.) or completion. The building official shall inspect at various intervals, and a final inspection of every building and system upon completion, prior to certificate of occupancy or completion.
(5) Posting permit. Work shall not commence until the permit is posted conspicuously on the premises, protected from the weather, to permit the building official make the required entries. This permit shall be maintained until the C.O. or completion.
(6) Required inspections. The building official shall make the following inspections, and others as necessary, and release that portion of the construction or notify the permit holder/agent of any violations to be corrected:
a. Building.
1. Foundation and foundation wall: when trenches are excavated, reinforcement is in place, and forms erected, prior to concrete.
2. Slab: prior to concrete.
3. Frame: when roof, framing, fireblocking, bracing, fasteners, concealed wiring, pipes, chimneys, ducts and vents are complete.
4. Moisture barrier: prior to the install of the exterior finishing.
5. Final: when the building is complete and ready for occupancy.
b. Electrical.
1. Underground: when trenches or ditches are excavated, conduit or cable installed, before any backfilling.
2. Rough-in: when the roof, framing, fireblocking, and bracing is in place and prior to the installation of wall or ceiling membranes.
3. Final: when the building is complete, all electrical fixtures are in place and connected, and the structure is ready for occupancy.
c. Plumbing.
1. Underground: when trenches or ditches are excavated, piping installed, before any backfilling.
2. Rough-in: when the roof, framing, fireblocking, bracing and soil, waste, and vent piping are done, before wall or ceiling membranes.
3. Final: when the building is complete, all plumbing fixtures are connected, and the structure is ready for occupancy.
4. Note: See section 312 of International Plumbing Code for required tests.
d. Mechanical.
1. Underground: when trenches/ditches are excavated, underground duct and fuel piping installed, before any backfilling.
2. Rough-in: when the roof, framing, fireblocking, bracing and all ducting, and other concealed components are complete, prior to installation of wall or ceiling membranes.
3. Final: when the building is complete, the mechanical system is connected, and the structure is ready for occupancy.
e. Gas.
1. Rough piping: when all new piping is installed, before piping is covered/concealed or fixtures or appliances connected.
2. Final piping: when all piping authorized is installed, after all portions to be concealed are concealed, before any fixtures or appliances connected. This shall include a pressure test.
3. Final: To be made on all new gas work and existing systems affected by new work or any changes, to ensure compliance with all the codes and to ensure that the gas system is per reviewed plans.
f. Energy.
1. Foundation: before slab concrete is poured, to verify perimeter insulation has been installed correctly.
2. Frame: before exterior wall insulation is concealed, to check the insulation and confirm all holes and cracks through the structure envelope have been sealed appropriately to restrict air passage.
3. Final: when the building is complete and ready for occupancy, to verify installation and R-value of ceiling and floor insulation and verify correct SEER ratings on appliances.
(7) Release. Work shall not be done on any part of a building or system beyond the point indicated in each successive inspection without a written release from the building official. Such release shall be only after an inspection of each successive step as indicated by each of the foregoing inspections.
(8) Reinforcing steel, structural frames, insulation, plumbing, mechanical, or electrical systems. No such systems or work shall be covered or concealed without first obtaining a release from the building official.
(9) Plaster fire protection. Where plaster is used for fire protection, the permit holder shall notify the building official after lathing and backing. Plaster shall not be applied until release from the building official.
(i) Certificates.
(1) Certificate of occupancy.
a. Building occupancy. A building shall not be occupied or a change made in occupancy, nature, or use of a building or part thereof until after the building official issues a C.O. It shall not issue until all systems have been inspected for compliance with the codes and other laws and ordinances and released by the building official.
b. Issuing C.O. Upon satisfactory completion of construction per the codes, plans and specifications, and after final inspection, the building official shall issue a C.O. stating nature of the occupancy permitted, number of persons for each floor, and allowable load per square foot for each floor per the codes.
c. Temporary occupancy. A temporary C.O. may issue for a portion of a commercial building, which in the opinion of the building official, may safely be occupied prior to final completion. The temporary C.O. shall be forfeited if the final C.O. is not issued within 90 days.
d. Existing building C.O. A C.O. for an existing building may be sought by making application to the building official, who may require two sets of drawings, or a general inspection, or both. If the building conforms to the codes and applicable laws and ordinances, a C.O. shall be issued.
(2) Certificate of completion. Upon satisfactory completion of a building or system, a certificate of completion may be issued, as proof that it is released for connection to a utility system. This does not grant authority to occupy a building prior to C.O.
(3) Service utilities.
a. Connection. No one shall connect from a utility to a building or system, until release by the building official and a certificate of occupancy or completion.
b. Temporary. The building official may authorize temporary connection of a building or system to a utility for testing systems under a temporary C.O.
c. Disconnect. The building official may authorize disconnection of utility service in case of emergency to eliminate a hazard. The building official shall try to notify the utility and, when possible, the owner and occupant, of the decision to disconnect prior to such. If not notified prior to disconnecting, the owner or occupant shall be notified as soon as practical thereafter.
(j) Floor loads.
(1) Occupancy. A building shall not have floors loaded beyond safe capacity. Occupancy is allowed only when the building official is satisfied capacity will not be exceeded.
(2) Storage, factory-industrial, etc., occupancies. The owner or occupant of any building where excessive floor loading may occur, shall employ a competent architect or engineer in computing safe load capacity. Such computations shall be filed, accompanied by an affidavit from the architect or engineer stating safe allowable floor load on each floor in pounds per square foot uniformly distributed.
(3) Signs. In every building or part thereof used for storage, industrial, or hazardous purposes, the safe floor loads, approved by the building official, shall be marked on plates and securely affixed by the owner conspicuously in each story. Such shall not be removed or defaced, and if removed or defaced, shall be replaced by the owner.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(7))
401:
The building official may require test reports as proof of compliance. Tests are at the expense of the owner or agent, by an approved testing lab or other approved agency.
(Ord. of 12-18-2019(3), art. 2(8))
402:
(a) Council. The council shall have the power to hear appeals of decisions and interpretations of the building official and consider variances.
(b) Appeals process.
(1) Decision of building official. The owner of a building or system may appeal a decision of the building official to the council whenever any one of the following conditions are claimed to exist:
a. The building official rejected or refused to approve the construction proposed or materials to be used in a building or service system.
b. The provisions of the codes do not apply to this specific case.
c. That an equally good or more desirable installation can be employed.
d. The intent of the codes or regulations have been incorrectly interpreted.
(2) Variances. The council, after a hearing, may vary the application of the codes when enforcement thereof would do manifest injustice contrary to the spirit and purpose of the codes or public interest, and also finds all of the following:
a. Special conditions and circumstances peculiar and unique to this building or system exist and do not result from action or inaction of applicant.
b. A variance will not confer on applicant any special privilege denied to others.
c. The variance is the minimum to allow reasonable use of the building/system.
d. The variance will be in harmony with the general intent and purpose of the codes and not detrimental to public health, safety, and welfare.
The council may prescribe a reasonable time limit within which the action for which the variance is required shall be commenced and completed, and may prescribe conditions and safeguards in conformity with the codes. Violation of the conditions of a variance shall be deemed a violation of the codes.
(3) Notice of appeal. Appeal shall be filed in writing within 30 days after the building official's decision, in a form acceptable to the building official.
(4) Unsafe or dangerous buildings or systems. If a building or system, in the opinion of the building official, is unsafe, unsanitary, or dangerous, the building official may limit the time for such appeal to a shorter period.
(c) Decisions. Council shall reach a decision, with the reasons, without unreasonable delay and file it in writing in the office of the building official, open to public inspection. If a decision reverses or modifies the building official or varies the application of any provision of the codes, the building official shall act per such decision. A certified copy of the decision shall be sent to the appellant. Every decision shall be final, subject to non de novo, certiorari appeal to superior court.

403:
A person or entity who shall violate the codes, or erect, construct, alter, install, demolish, or move a structure or system in violation of a statement or drawing or plan, shall be guilty of an ordinance violation. It is a separate offense for each and every day or portion thereof during which any violation continues, and upon conviction, shall be punished as provided by this Code.
